Everything below is something the workshop actually leans on — a book it
assumes, a paper a section implements, a library it tells you to use instead of
your own code. Nothing is here to pad a bibliography.

Read it two ways. **Before or during the session**, it is where a term you have
just met is defined properly. **After it**, it is the ladder out: the survey
first, then whichever of the four papers covers the decomposition you ended up
needing.

{{< include _includes/references-en.md >}}

## Not on this page {#elsewhere}

- **[Prerequisites](index.qmd#prerequisites)** — the pre-work, in full, on the
  homepage. That is the one list to work through *before* the session; this
  page is for after it.
- **[The handbook](tensors_workshop_plan_with_quizzes.md)** — the workshop's
  own text, including the five take-home appendices. It cites the works above
  where each one is first needed.
- **[The machine-generated companion](companion.qmd)** — a video, infographics,
  an audio overview, a quiz, flashcards and a mind map, all generated by
  NotebookLM from this workshop's own sources. It is *generated, not written*:
  use it as a second pass, and check anything it asserts against the works on
  this page rather than the other way round.
